LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_Locked: The ink is dry: it has been sent.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_Preamble: The undersigned, speaking for {0} and for {1}, being of sound mind and mostly sober, and wishing that fewer of their people be shot by the other's, do agree as follows.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_OpenEnded: This treaty holds until either party ends it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_Sweetener_Desc: Silver handed over if, and only if, they sign. Greedy governments are swayed more by it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_Press_Desc: Spend extra influence leaning on their officials: a little better odds, spent whatever they answer.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_Bill: Sending it costs {0} influence, whatever the answer. Silver ({1}) changes hands only if they sign.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_SignAndSend_Desc: Put your name to it and send it to {0}. They will seal it, refuse it, or name a price.
LanguageData.Dominion_Paper_CounterText: {0} will sign, they say, for another {1} silver ({2} in all). Their envoy is smiling in a way you do not like.
LanguageData.Dominion_Odds_OpinionTooLow: They will not even read it: their opinion of you ({0}) is below {1}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Odds_TooFar: Too far away: they only sign this with neighbours within {0} tiles.
LanguageData.Dominion_Odds_ShortTerm: a short term asks less of them
LanguageData.Dominion_Odds_LongTerm: a long term asks more of them
LanguageData.Dominion_Odds_WarScore: how the war is going for them
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Search_Desc: Type part of a faction's name to find it.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Sort_Desc: Order the list. Pinned factions always come first.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Pin: Pin to the top of the list
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_SortBy: Click to sort by {0}; click again to reverse.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_MapLegend: Large dots: {0}. Tint: spheres of influence; red borders: fronts. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a town to pick its faction, right-click for more.
LanguageData.Dominion_Map_RightClick: Right-click: show it on the world map, or open its pages.
LanguageData.Dominion_Map_ZoomIn: Zoom in (or scroll the mouse wheel over the map).
LanguageData.Dominion_Map_Help: Scroll to zoom, drag to pan. The map wraps round east to west. Each faction's sphere of influence is tinted in its colour; borders between factions at war are drawn in red as fronts.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Jump_Dossier_Desc: Open {0}'s dossier in the Overview tab.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Jump_War_Desc: Show the War tab with {0}'s wars first.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Jump_Intel_Desc: Open the intelligence service's file on {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_UI_Jump_Map_Desc: Find {0}'s capital on the world map.
LanguageData.Dominion_Treaties_Draft_Desc: Open the signing desk: pick a partner and a treaty, set its terms and sign.
LanguageData.Dominion_Treaties_NoneYours: You are party to no treaties. The desk is empty and the ink is fresh.
LanguageData.Dominion_Treaties_WebHelp: Hover a faction to light up its treaties; click it to keep it lit. Only treaties your intelligence knows of are shown.
LanguageData.Dominion_Treaty_Renew_Desc: Back to the signing desk: renew it, or change its term, with {0}. It then runs from today. Renewing a treaty that works is easier than signing a new one.
LanguageData.Dominion_Treaty_NoLongerInForce: That treaty is no longer in force.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_0_Desc: Half the usual term. Easier to agree to.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_1_Desc: The usual term for this treaty.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_2_Desc: Twice the usual term. Harder to agree to, but you will not be back at the desk for a while.
LanguageData.Dominion_TreatyExpiring_Text: The {0} with {1} lapses in {2} days. Renew it at the signing desk, or let it go.
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Alliance: The parties are allies, in war and in peace.
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_NonAggression: Neither party shall take up arms against the other.
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Defensive: Each party comes to the other's defence if it is attacked.
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Trade: Trade between the parties is cheaper both ways ({0}).
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Intel: The parties share what they know (+{0} intel on the partner).
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Puppet: {0} is a protectorate of {1}, and follows it to war.
LanguageData.Dominion_Provision_Federation: Membership of the Federation, with its rights and its dues.
LanguageData.Dominion_TearUp_Grievance: {0} will hold a grievance for it.
LanguageData.Dominion_TearUp_Violation: This is a violation, not a notice: {0} and everyone watching will think less of you.
LanguageData.Dominion_Dip_Desk_Desc: Your best leadership desk. Advanced diplomacy needs one, and a head of state.
LanguageData.Dominion_Dip_Comms_Desc: A powered comms console lets you send basic diplomacy without a desk.
LanguageData.Dominion_Dip_History_Desc: Everything you did toward this faction, what came of it, and what they did to you.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Tip: Sent as an envoy's letter: choose its tone before you seal it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_SealAndSend_Desc: Sign it, press your seal into the wax and send it to {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Delivered: The letter was delivered to {0}. Whether it was read is another matter.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tone_Warm_Desc: Friendly words. Gestures of goodwill count for more, if they do not already loathe you; insults lose their bite.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tone_Formal_Desc: Correct, cold and safe. No bonus, no risk.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tone_Threatening_Desc: A veiled threat. Demands work better when you are the stronger; friendly gestures are spoiled, insults cut deeper, and they will resent it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Tone_Warm_Effect: Warm: goodwill earned ×1.25; better odds unless they already despise you; hostile words sting less (×0.6).
LanguageData.Dominion_Tone_Threatening_Effect: Threatening: demands gain from your strength; goodwill earned ×0.5; hostile words sting more (×1.5); they gain a small grievance.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Closing_Warm: With every good wish for your health and harvest,
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Closing_Threatening: We trust you will not make us write again,
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Gift_Warm: Friends! Please accept these {2} silver from the people of {3}, with our warmest thoughts. Spend it on something nice. Or on walls. We do not judge.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Gift_Formal: The government of {3} presents {2} silver to the government of {0}, as a token of regard.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Gift_Threatenin: Here are {2} silver. Consider what else we could afford to send, and in which direction.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Compliment_Warm: We have long admired the people of {0}: your craftsmanship, your courage, and the remarkable state of your roads. It is an honour to be your neighbours.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Compliment_Form: The government of {3} notes with approval the good order of {0} and the wise leadership of {1}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Compliment_Thre: Your settlements are very well built. It would be a shame if anything happened to them. We say this as an admirer.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Insult_Warm: With the greatest affection, we must observe that your soup is thin, your banners are faded and your leader's hat is a matter of public concern.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Insult_Formal: The government of {3} regards the conduct of {0} as beneath the standards of civilised peoples, and of most uncivilised ones.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Insult_Threaten: {1}, your people are cowards, your walls are sand and your mother was a muffalo. Come and dispute it, if you dare.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Denounce_Warm: It pains us, as friends of all peoples, to say publicly that the conduct of {0} has been unworthy of them. We hope they will do better.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Denounce_Formal: Let it be known to every government on the planet that {3} formally denounces {0} and its actions.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_Denounce_Threat: We denounce {0} before the whole world, and we are keeping a list. You are at the top of it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_DemandTribute_W: As good neighbours who keep the roads safe for you, we would be grateful for a modest contribution toward the cost. Whatever you think fair.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_DemandTribute_F: The government of {3} requests that {0} pay a tribute in recognition of the present balance of power.
LanguageData.Dominion_Letter_Dominion_DemandTribute_T: Pay. Our soldiers are bored, and bored soldiers wander. They might wander as far as your granaries.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Gift: If received: goodwill and favour, more for bigger gifts. The silver goes into their treasury.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Compliment: If it lands: a little goodwill and favour. If it falls flat: slightly less favour.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Insult: Always lands: goodwill and favour lost, and a grievance gained.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_ProposePeace: Opens the peace table, where you draft the terms.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_DeclareWar: War, with the goal you choose. Every treaty with them is broken.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_ProposeTreaty: Opens the signing desk, where you set the terms.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Borders: Changes who may cross your land, and what it costs them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Embargo: Stops (or restarts) trade with them; it hurts their economy and yours.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_Denounce: Everyone hears of it: their reputation suffers and so do your relations.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_DemandTribute: If they fold: silver now and a lasting grievance. If not: lost favour and a grievance anyway.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_HostageExchang: Trust on both sides, held by the people you trade.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_ProposeSummit: Their leader visits your capital for talks with your head of state.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_CallToArms: Asks them to join your war.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_ColdWar: Open hostility short of war, or an end to it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Outcome_Dominion_ProxyWar: Silver to their enemies, so others do your fighting.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_Weariness_Desc: How sick of the war {0} is. Weary governments make peace more readily.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_Casualties_Desc: People killed on each side (yours first, theirs second) since the war began {0} ago. {1} battles fought.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_PeaceTable_Desc: Draft a peace: victor's terms, or a deal over settlements, silver and prisoners.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_Mercenaries_Desc: Pay a free company to raid the enemy: war score now, their army worn down and their nerve shaken. Once every {0} days.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_Chronicle_Desc: The war's history: battles, captures, orders and how the score stood after each.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_ChronicleEmpty: Nothing has happened yet. Wars are mostly waiting.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_ReadStory: Click to read the newspaper's story.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarTab_NoStory: No story about this has reached your paper.
LanguageData.Dominion_Stance_Balanced_Desc: Fight the war as it comes. No bonus, no cost.
LanguageData.Dominion_Stance_Aggressive_Desc: Press every advantage: your successes count 30% more toward the war score, but your setbacks count 15% more too.
LanguageData.Dominion_Stance_Defensive_Desc: Dig in: your setbacks count 30% less, your successes 15% less.
LanguageData.Dominion_Stance_RaidSupply_Desc: Go after their supply lines: every day their economy and nerve suffer a little. Your own successes count 10% less.
LanguageData.Dominion_Mercenaries_Hired: Mercenaries paid {0} silver raided {1}: +{2} war score.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_Facts: {0} of war, {1} battles. Your dead: {2}. Dead of {4}: {3}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_Victors_Desc: You are winning: take what you went to war for ({0}), as the war score allows.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_Negotiated_Desc: Set the terms yourself: who keeps which settlement, silver either way, prisoners freed. The odds follow what you ask.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_NotWinning: You need a lead of {0} war score to dictate terms.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_Bill: Proposing it costs {0} influence, whatever they answer. Silver is paid when the peace is made.
LanguageData.Dominion_Peace_Sign_Desc: Sign these terms and send them to {0}.
LanguageData.Dominion_Deal_Keep_Desc: You hold it now. Keeping it makes peace harder; giving it back makes it easier.
LanguageData.Dominion_Deal_DemandBack_Desc: They hold it now. Demanding it makes peace harder; letting them keep it makes it easier.
LanguageData.Dominion_Deal_NoOccupied: Neither side holds the other's settlements.
LanguageData.Dominion_Deal_ReleasePrisoners_Desc: Prisoners of theirs held at your colony walk free when the peace is made. They will remember it kindly.
LanguageData.Dominion_Deal_NoPrisoners: You hold none of their people.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_ClickForFloor: Click to see how every member leans on it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Tally_Desc: Votes for (green) and against (red), weighted. A motion carries with more for than against and at least {0} for: a third of the room.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Gavel_Desc: Close the debate and count the votes. There is no going back.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Adjourn_Desc: The session is over. Decrees passed are now in force.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_LobbyHint: Lobby members who waver, or who lean the other way. Each member can be lobbied once per motion.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Lobby_Desc: Work on {0}'s delegate: with influence, silver or a promise.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_LobbySilver: A discreet purse: {0} silver ({1} chance, sways them more)
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_LobbyPromise: Promise to back their next motion ({0} chance; break it and they will not forget)
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_PromiseOwnMotion: They sponsor this motion; a promise would be broken the moment you vote.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_AlreadyPromised: You already owe them a promise.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_PromiseKept: You kept your promise to {0} on "{1}".
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_PromiseBroken: You broke your promise to {0} on "{1}". They will remember.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Forecast_Desc: How it would go today without your vote. Delegates still on the road are not counted.
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_InGrace: members still have time to comply
LanguageData.Dominion_Council_Weight_Desc: Voting weight: bigger, richer and stronger members weigh more, and allies in the room add a little.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Screen_Operations_Desc: Missions under way. Click one to open its file.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Screen_Board_Desc: What the service knows about each faction, and what is still redacted.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Screen_Counter_Desc: Foreign services working against you, and sweeps to catch them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Screen_Archive_Desc: Finished missions and how they ended.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_NoOps: NO OPERATIONS RUNNING. THE AGENTS ARE PLAYING CARDS.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Recall_Desc: Call the agents home now. Nothing comes of the mission and nothing is refunded.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_RecallConfirm: Recall the agents on "{0}" against {1}? The mission is abandoned and what it cost is lost.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_NothingToLocate: Nothing of it is on a map you can see.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_NoSuspicions: NOTHING SUSPICIOUS. WHICH IS ITSELF SUSPICIOUS.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_Sweep_Desc: Spend {0} influence turning the colony over for {1}'s agents. Caught: their file on you shrinks and everyone hears of it. Missed: the trail cools.
LanguageData.Dominion_Term_TheirFiles_Desc: How much each foreign service knows about your colony. You can only see this with intel of {0} or more on them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ops_CannotRecallPhysical: Agents on the ground must finish or flee on their own.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ops_Recalled: The agents on "{0}" against {1} have been recalled.
LanguageData.Dominion_Ops_SweepMissed: The sweep found nothing of {0}'s agents. The trail has gone cold.
LanguageData.Dominion_Mission_Handler_Desc: A colonist who runs the mission from home: adds a little of their skill and does not leave the colony.
LanguageData.Dominion_Mission_Exposure: Chance of being caught: {0} if it fails, {1} even if it works.
LanguageData.Dominion_Risk_Cautious_Desc: Slow and careful: 10% worse odds and a quarter longer, but half as likely to be caught.
LanguageData.Dominion_Risk_Bold_Desc: Fast and loud: 10% better odds and a quarter shorter, but 60% more likely to be caught.
LanguageData.Dominion_Road_Step0_Desc: Open the research tab to study Planetary Federation.
LanguageData.Dominion_Road_Step1_Desc: Propose the Federation Charter at the Rim Council and see it passed.
LanguageData.Dominion_Road_Step2_Desc: Bring factions in: invite them to join, make them your protectorates, or conquer them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_ReadCharter_Desc: The Federation's founding charter, with the seal of every member.
LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_Invite_Desc: Offer a faction membership of the Federation, at the signing desk.
LanguageData.Dominion_Federation_Loyalty_Desc: Their opinion of you. Members who come to resent you may walk out, more so under heavy dues.
LanguageData.Dominion_Dues_1_Desc: {0} silver a time; they grumble a little
LanguageData.Dominion_Dues_2_Desc: {0} silver a time; they resent it, and a resentful member may leave
LanguageData.Dominion_Dues_Desc: What this member pays toward the Federation every {0} days, delivered to your capital.
LanguageData.Dominion_Dues_LeftText: {0} has had enough of your dues and your manner, and has left the Federation.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Preamble: We, the peoples of this world, having fought over every hill and well and sometimes over nothing at all, and having noticed that the raiders keep coming regardless, join together under the leadership of {0} to make something larger than ourselves.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Article1: The members are one Federation. An attack on one is an attack on all, and so is an insult, within reason.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Article2: No member shall make war on another. Disputes go to the council, and to the council's very patient secretary.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Article3: Caravans of members travel freely and trade fairly. Muffalo are counted once, at the border.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Article4: Members contribute to the common purse as the founding member sets, and complain about it as is their right.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_Article5: Any member may leave. It will be remembered.
LanguageData.Dominion_Charter_NotInForce: The charter is drafted but not yet in force: it needs the research and the council's vote.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_Search_Desc: Find stories by any word in the headline or text, or by a faction's name.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_View_Desc: Which stories to show: the latest, your bookmarks, a past day's paper, or your scrapbook.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_View_Latest_Desc: everything, newest first, bookmarks on top
LanguageData.Dominion_News_View_Scrapbook_Desc: stories you clipped out and kept
LanguageData.Dominion_News_Pick: Tick to act on several stories at once.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_BatchRespond_Desc: Give the radio desk one order for every ticked story it applies to. The desk holds {0} orders at a time.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_BatchTitle: The radio desk has room for {0} more orders
LanguageData.Dominion_News_BatchQueued: {0} orders to {1} queued at the radio desk.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_BatchQueuedFull: {0} orders to {1} queued; {2} more did not fit, as the desk is full.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_BatchRead_Desc: Mark the ticked stories as read.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_Bookmark_Desc: Star it: bookmarked stories stay at the top and are never thrown out with old news.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_Clip_Desc: Clip it out for your scrapbook. Clipped stories are kept forever.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_Unclip: Take it out of the scrapbook
LanguageData.Dominion_News_ScrapbookEmpty: Your scrapbook is empty. Clip stories out with the scissors at the top of an article.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_FactionLink: Click for {0}'s dossier, diplomacy or capital.
LanguageData.Dominion_News_JumpPlace: Click to find {0} on the world map.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_Status: Your wars: {0} · wars abroad you know of: {1} · warbands marching on you: {2}
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_Alarm: {0} warband(s) are marching on your settlements. Open the theatre report or watch the map.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_Quiet: No warband is marching on you.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_Unknown: {0} more war(s) your intelligence knows nothing about.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_Theatre_Desc: Everything moving in the world: warbands in the field, cold wars, occupied settlements and blockades. The map shows every war you know of.
LanguageData.Dominion_WarRoom_OpenDossier: Click to open this war's dossier and put it on the map.
LanguageData.Dominion_Telegraph_TapeEmpty: The wire is quiet. Your messages to other factions, and theirs to you, will print here.
LanguageData.Dominion_Telegraph_TapeTip: A wire to or from {0}. Click to open their line. The tape stops while you read it.
LanguageData.Dominion_Telegraph_Goodwill_Desc: {0}'s goodwill toward you, as the game counts it: it decides whether they are hostile, neutral or allied.
LanguageData.Dominion_Telegraph_TheirOpinion_Desc: What {0} actually thinks of you, from everything that has passed between you. The faint blue needle is your view of them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_Mode_Shelves_Desc: Every treaty you are party to, as a scroll on the shelves. The ribbon's colour is the kind of treaty; a frayed ribbon means it lapses within 15 days. Pull a scroll out to unroll it on the desk.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_Mode_Records_Desc: Index cards for treaties between other factions that your intelligence knows of.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_Mode_Corkboard_Desc: Every faction you know pinned to cork, with a string for each treaty between them.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_PullOut: Click to pull it out and unroll it on the desk; click again to put it back.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_DeskEmpty: Pull a scroll from the shelves to read it here.
LanguageData.Dominion_Archive_CannotRenew: This treaty does not lapse, or was imposed on the losing side, so there is nothing to renew.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_NoSession: Motions can only be put on the agenda once a session has been announced.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_NoMotions: The session is announced, but nothing is on the agenda yet.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_NoAgenda: The council is in recess. When a session is announced, its motions will hang here.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_ClickBanner: Click to colour the seats by how each member leans on this motion.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_Empty: The council has no members yet.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_YourVote: You cast your own vote when the session opens.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_LobbyHint: You can lobby undecided members on the ballot once the session opens.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_ClickSeat: Click to see this member beside the chamber.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_InSessionSoon: A session is called, hosted by {0}. Hang a motion on the rail or study the room.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_LegendFactions: Seats in members' colours, in proportion to vote weight. Pick a banner to see how they lean.
LanguageData.Dominion_Chamber_PickSeat: Click a seat in the chamber to see that member: their weight, attendance and how they lean on each motion.
